limits: PHP substitutes persistent constants such as NAN and PHP_INT_MAX while compiling; Phego leaves them for execution, so [NAN . ''] lacks its compile warning. Excluded from the fixture and listed in engineering/decisions/compatibility-php8512.md.
SPL classes such as ArrayObject have no inheritance metadata before W-29; static covariance cases use equivalent user classes.
Constant expressions fold a class operand before PHP checks it, so const X = (A::class)::C; and const X = (PHP_EOL)::C; compile in PHP but not in Phego.
Closures inside attribute arguments are checked as constant expressions but their bodies are not lowered, so their compile-time diagnostics are missing.

Inheritance errors follow child method order and name the earliest ancestor; PHP follows parent order, reports properties first and names the nearest override. $a[] ??= 1 and multi-line virtual hook lines also differ.
Lower returns only the CompileError on a compile failure, so warnings PHP prints before the fatal error are not available to the caller; W-17 decides the error display path.
A parenthesized right-nested constant expression deeper than 2,048 levels, or a superlinear operation beyond the unit's shared reserve, reports a host resource limit; PHP compiles it.
PHP substitutes class constants while compiling (zend_try_ct_eval_class_const); Phego leaves them for execution, so $o->{self::K} with const K = [1] lacks its Array to string conversion warning.
Constant expression contains invalid operations uses the offending node's line; PHP uses the current compile line, which differs for multi-line expressions (main shares this).
PHP accepts \self::class as self::class; Phego still reports '\self' is an invalid class name while lowering, as main does.

(PHP_EOL)::C in a constant expression compiles in PHP because persistent constants are substituted; Phego reports a dynamic class name like PHP does for (A)::C. main accepts both because it has no check. Needs a builtin constant table.
review_status: All nine PR #129 review comments on 3da26d5 were reproduced with the pinned images and fixed with failing-first regression cases. Independent adversarial reviews of dc2b04f, c98cc07, a828a53 and 0ba11a8 found regressions against main and same-pattern gaps; they are fixed with new cases. The remaining differences either exist on main or need new features, and are listed in limits; by the user's decision of 2026-11-07 they do not block merging.
